question: Can a detector trained to distinguish architectural doors from furniture doors authorize a room-door parent with an enclosed handle while rejecting handled cabinets, closets, and large doorless openings?
single_change_from_pb11: Replace depth-only planar closure with a learned RGB semantic part-parent graph whose competing parent classes are door, cabinet door, and refrigerator door.

information_source.source_disjoint_boundary: The named DoorDetect Dataset training source is distinct from SUN RGB-D. Exact cross-source image-hash exclusion is not claimed because the original training image tree is no longer present at its manifest-era path.

representation.input: Each full source RGB image once at 640 square inference; no crops, tiles, depth, augmentation, class filtering, or test-time ensemble.
representation.assignment: Assign each handle to the smallest-area enclosing parent box; break ties by higher parent confidence, lower class index, then lexicographic box coordinates.
representation.authorization: At least one handle must be assigned to a class-0 door parent. Cabinet-door and refrigerator-door parents compete and cannot authorize.

frame_attribution.result: The visible room-door handle was detected at confidence 0.6644, but no door parent was detected around it. Four cabinet-door panels and their handles were separately classified and assigned correctly.

Door, handle, and overlapping cabinet-door boxes were detected. The handle center lay just outside the door box but inside the cabinet-door box, so the frozen rule assigned it to cabinet door and rejected the frame.
Only a refrigerator-door false parent was retained; no handle was detected.
The red architectural door was detected at confidence 0.4428, but its visible handle was not detected.
No detection survived, so the mail-room cabinet was correctly not authorized.
The sliding closet produced multiple cabinet-door and handle detections; enclosed handles were assigned to cabinet-door parents and the frame was correctly not authorized.
Neither large opening produced a retained detection or authorization.

attribution.positive_signal: The source learned meaningful part semantics: it found architectural door parents on 2/4 positives, a visible architectural-door handle on 2/4, dense cabinet-door/handle structure on the strongest furniture controls, and rejected both large openings.
attribution.decisive_failure: Parent and child recall did not co-occur reliably on any of the four real doors. One real door also received overlapping door and cabinet-door parent hypotheses whose frozen enclosure geometry favored the wrong semantic parent.
attribution.failure_layer: The bottleneck is the detector's box-level part/parent representation and cross-domain semantic calibration, not the absence of all door-part evidence and not the large-opening rejection rule.
closed: This frozen YOLO11n checkpoint plus center-in-smallest-parent topology on the consumed PB12 cohort
Any rescue by confidence, image size, NMS, crop, tile, area, overlap, parent priority, alternate epoch, checkpoint, YOLO size, or fusion on these pixels
attribution.next_information_needed: A distinct pixel-level door-part source that can localize leaf, frame, handle, and furniture-door competitors without depending on overlapping whole-object boxes.

execution_recovery.attempt_1: Inference completed in memory, but the evaluator rejected Ultralytics synthetic batch display path image0.jpg before writing a result. No detections or metrics were shown to the operator and no result file existed.
execution_recovery.mechanical_change: Removed only the non-scoring backend display-path assertion and retained positional result binding to the same frozen ordered and hashed input list.
execution_recovery.attempt_2: One unchanged mechanical replay created the formal result. Protocol, cohort, checkpoint, inference parameters, topology, and gate were unchanged.

protocol_outcome.required_action: Close the checkpoint/topology pair on this cohort and change the information source or representation.

next_step: Run one fresh, pre-frozen pixel-level door-part topology Development test with a distinct information source. Do not tune or fuse the PB12 detector on its consumed pixels.
claim_boundary: PB12 is a fresh Development falsification of one frozen RGB detector/topology pair. It does not reject door-part models generally and establishes no exact target ownership, public access, open or closed actuation state, traversability, active-view causality, temporal persistence, guidance, arrival, product benefit, user benefit, or safety authority.
